subject: Implementing the RW2 model in rgeneric gives different results

messages.author: 1475e652f3d71feb
messages.subject: Implementing the RW2 model in rgeneric gives different results
parts:
Hi,

I am currently looking to implement the rw2 model component using the rgeneric framework. Unfortunately the estimates are quite different compared to using the built-in "rw2" model component. They also seem to be more unstable and sometimes change whenever if I rerun INLA. I haven't had issues with rgeneric implementations of other model components. 

I also tested this using some (very) old code from when I managed to implement this successfully, but this now also runs into similar issues.

Has there been some changes to rgeneric that I have missed, that could cause issues with the rw2 model?

Here is the example I have been running, which is slightly edited from the 'inla.doc("rw2")' example. 
set.seed(123)
  n = 100
  z = seq(0, 6, length.out=n)
  y = sin(z)+rnorm(n, mean=0, sd=0.5)
  data = data.frame(y=y, z=z, idz=1:n)
  formula = y~f(idz,model="rw2")
  r = inla(formula,data=data,family="gaussian")

  rw2model = inla.rgeneric.define(rgeneric.rw2, n=n)
  formula = y ~ f(idz, model=rw2model)
  rr = inla(formula, data=data, family="gaussian")

  print(r$summary.hyperpar$mean[2])
> 8341.309
  print(inla.emarginal(function(x)exp(x),rr$marginals.hyperpar$`Theta1 for idz`))
> 57.00625

Here is the rgeneric model implementation, in case it would be helpful:

rgeneric.rw2 = function(
    cmd = c("graph", "Q","mu", "initial", "log.norm.const", "log.prior", "quit"),
    theta = NULL)
{
  envir = parent.env(environment())

  interpret.theta = function() {
    params = list(kappa=exp(theta[1]))
    return(params)
  }

  mu = function() {
    return(numeric(0))
  }

  graph = function(){
    G = Q()
    G[G != 0] = 1
    return (G)
  }

  Q = function(){
    if(!is.null(envir)){
      nn=get("n",envir)
    }
    params = interpret.theta()

    ii = c(1:nn,1:(nn-1),1:(nn-2))
    jj = c(1:nn, 2:nn, 3:nn)
    xx = params$kappa *c(1,5,rep(6,nn-4),5,1,-2,rep(-4,nn-3),-2,rep(1,nn-2))

    QQ = Matrix::sparseMatrix(i=ii,j=jj,x=xx,symmetric=TRUE)
    return ( QQ )
  }

  log.norm.const = function(){
    return(numeric(0))
  }

  log.prior = function(){
    params = interpret.theta()
    lprior = dgamma(params$kappa, shape=1, rate=0.0001, log=TRUE) + log(params$kappa)
    return (lprior)
  }

  initial = function(){
    return (c(4))
    }

  quit = function(){
    return ()
    }

  if (!length(theta)) theta = initial()

  cmd = match.arg(cmd)
  val = do.call(cmd, args = list())
  return (val)
}

I would be very grateful for any clarifying comments.

Many thanks in advance,

Eirik
